posts.caption: In 2021, one engineer typed one wrong command and 3.5 billion people lost the internet in a single instant. Not hacked. Not attacked. Just one wrong line of code during a routine maintenance check. Facebook's own engineers couldn't even log in to fix it, their access tools were on the same servers that just vanished. They had to physically drive to data centers and override servers by hand. One by one. 6 hours. $60 million lost every single hour. And the exact same vulnerability? Still exists right now. The internet is more fragile than you think.

2021 mein ek engineer ne ek galat command type ki aur 3.5 billion logon ka internet ek pal mein band ho gaya. Hack nahi hua. Attack nahi hua. Bas ek routine maintenance check ke dauran ek galat line of code. 6 ghante. Har ghante 60 million dollar ka nuksaan. Internet utna strong nahi jitna hum sochte hain.

There is a sound that only 2% of people can hear. Scientists have studied it for 50 years and still have no answer. It's called The Hum — and the leading theory is that it's the Earth itself vibrating at a frequency most humans aren't built to detect. A woman heard it for 11 years, moved across the country to escape it, and it followed her to the new house. Stop right now, close your eyes, and listen. What do you hear?

We call space the final frontier. But we've barely explored our own planet. Earth is stranger than anything we've found out there — and most people have no idea. From perfect solar eclipses to oceans deeper than mountains are tall, this is the planet you thought you knew.

In 1974, a man calculated the exact day he would die and spent a year preparing for it. What happened next is stranger than the prediction itself. Frank was obsessed with numerology. He told his family, quit his job, and gave away everything he owned. When the day came and went without incident, he thought he'd beaten fate. He hadn't.

recentPosts.caption: Observing the early universe would be such a fascinating and relaxing experience... or would it be?

We imagine advanced alien civilizations building gigantic spaceships, Dyson spheres and empires spanning entire galaxies. But what if true technological progress goes in exactly the opposite direction? Not outward into space, but deeper and deeper into the smallest layers of reality?

What is the Barrow Scale? How powerful could a civilization become by mastering DNA, and even fundamental particles, and could the universe already be filled with godlike civilizations hiding in plain sight? Watch
Let's visit some of the most dangerous neighbourhoods... in space!

Our curiosity to learn more about the stars is endless. Today, some scientists pursue their passion by building large telescopes that are able to capture the faintest glimmer of stars billions of light-years away. Some telescopes are even launched from Earth to get a clearer view outside the atmosphere. But what about the opportunity to see the stars with your own eyes, unfiltered? Astronauts, like the one that can be seen on the September page of our 12,026 Human Era calendar, say nothing compa

Could humans evolve to be able to fly some day? Flying like a bird would require way more than just wings. Hollow bones, giant chest muscles, rewired nerves, and absurd amounts of food might allow you to fly, but all of this would transform you into something barely human anymore.

In a battle against cancer, could viruses be our allies? When Croatian virologist Dr. Beata Halassy’s breast cancer returned for the third time, she made a bold decision: to experiment on herself using millions of viruses grown in her own lab. Viruses love cancer cells, which helped her turn them into a weapon against her own tumor.

What happens when you infect cancer with a virus, and could virotherapy become a powerful new tool against cancer? Watch our full video to find out!

What if continents and oceans switched places? The Pacific becomes a supercontinent. Earth's deepest point is Everest Deep, and is almost nine kilometers below sea-level. And the Mid-Atlantic Canyon divides the world from pole to pole. Life finds a way but struggles in this new, upside-down world. This all sounds cool, until the oxygen runs out.

Pigeons are basically GPS Drones with superpowers. They can pinpoint their own location hundreds of kilometers from their roosts and navigate home autonomously, only using smell, the Sun, and even Earth’s magnetic field.

No one works harder than our rover driver Yolk, who is tirelessly collecting nuggets every day so that the space station can function smoothly.

Have you already started your space adventure? Star Birds, which we developed together with our friends at @toukana_interactive, is available on Steam!
Two billion years ago, the world’s first nuclear reactors appeared in Oklo, Gabon. They were NOT made by humans and were self-regulating and accident-free.

In the late 9th century, Vikings have raided kingdom after kingdom and nearly conquered all of England. Wealthy monasteries and defenseless nuns were especially tempting targets and often suffered great losses. However, all of that stopped when Vikings were confronted by princess Aethelflaed, daughter of Alfred the Great.

Who was Lady of Mercia, and how did she shape the history of England by becoming Vikings' greatest nightmare? Watch our latest Nightshift video to find out! 🌚
Laughing gas can make you feel relaxed and euphoric in seconds. But it comes with serious risks as well. So, what exactly is laughing gas and why does it feel so good?

recentPosts.caption:
Nature creating its own little masterpiece. 🕷️🌅✨⁠
Neoscona crucifera carefully weaving its web, with the setting sun turning the delicate threads into a stunning mix of golden colors and intricate textures.⁠
⁠
Something so small, yet somehow capable of creating a view this beautiful. 🌿⁠
🎥: @angelazzarra

A stay that lets you experience Japan the traditional way. 🇯🇵✨⁠
Inside a traditional Japanese ryokan, where tatami rooms, peaceful surroundings, and classic Japanese hospitality come together with an incredible view of Mount Fuji. 🗻⁠
⁠
From sleeping on futons to enjoying the slower pace of a ryokan stay, it’s a beautiful way to experience a different side of Japan.⁠
And waking up to Fuji outside your window? That’s hard to beat. 🤍⁠
🎥: @dmytrosharapov

This café puts tiny edible ducks on its drinks. 🐥⁠
⁠
At Lu Cafe in Huế, Vietnam, drinks are served in crispy waffle cones and topped with tiny ducks that are actually edible.⁠
⁠
The playful drinks have been getting plenty of attention online, but we can see why. The little duck on top might be the cutest part.⁠
⁠
By: @lucafehue⁠

Somewhere that looks straight out of a fairytale. 🪷✨⁠
📍Usnisa Temple, Niushou Mountain, Nanjing is known for its spectacular Buddhist architecture, intricate details, and the impressive Usnisa Palace built into the mountain.⁠
And the experience doesn’t end with the views, visitors can leave a wish ribbon as a small personal blessing before heading back.⁠
⁠
Only about 1.5 hours from Shanghai by train, making it an easy day trip for something completely different.⁠
Would you make the trip for th

The beauty and diversity of Afghanistan, captured by Daniel Malikyar.⁠
⁠
“Afghanistan isn’t one identity, it’s many.” Through his portraits, the photographer documents some of the different ethnic groups he encountered while traveling across the country.⁠
⁠
His new book, 'Afghanistan', also brings together 130 photographs and personal essays, including a chapter dedicated to the country’s diversity.⁠
⁠
By: @dmalikyar

You do not need a big following to get paid for this. Here’s what it actually looks like when you start from zero.

1️⃣ Free stays first. Hotels have empty rooms every night and need content constantly. This is the easiest yes to get and it’s how most people start, because it costs the hotel nothing but an empty room.

2️⃣ Paid content for small businesses. One of our members filmed a restaurant he was already eating at, the video hit a million views, he went back and asked to be paid for the ne

This desert in Egypt looks like it’s covered in snow. ❄️⁠
⁠
The White Desert, located in Egypt’s Farafra region, is known for its strange white limestone formations scattered across the area.⁠
⁠
Wind erosion has shaped the soft rock into unusual forms, creating a landscape that almost looks frozen.⁠
⁠
By: @marcograssiphotography

A tattoo that carries much more than just a design. ✨🇹🇭⁠
@jazzywasinthailand experienced the ancient Thai tradition of Sak Yant, sacred tattoos traditionally created by Buddhist monks or spiritual practitioners and believed to offer blessings, protection, and guidance to those who receive them.⁠
⁠
More than an unforgettable travel experience, it’s a glimpse into a deeply rooted part of Thai spiritual and cultural traditions. 🙏⁠
Would you ever get a Sak Yant tattoo while traveling?

Vietnamese tequila… or snake wine? 🐍🥃😂⁠
One of Vietnam’s most unusual traditional drinks, rice wine infused with a snake, a practice traditionally associated with folk remedies and believed by some to have medicinal benefits.⁠
Whether you’re brave enough to try it or just curious about the taste, this is definitely one of those travel experiences you don’t forget.⁠
And apparently… it tastes pretty good. 👀⁠
⁠
Would you try it?⁠
🎥: @vanlifevibes.co

This road dives under the water so boats can pass right above it. 🚗🌊⁠
⁠
The Veluwemeer Aqueduct near Harderwijk, Netherlands, carries the N302 beneath a waterway, with around 3 meters of water above the road.⁠
⁠
Opened in 2002, the aqueduct lets cars and boats cross the same stretch without bridges, traffic lights, or stopping for each other.⁠
⁠
Video by: @themodernleper

Talk about having balance! 🐐⛰️⁠
The sight of an ibex navigating the rocky cliffs of Rocher du Vent in the Beaufortain Massif like it was the easiest thing in the world.⁠
Strong, sure-footed, and completely at home on terrain that would have most of us holding onto the railing. 😂⁠
⁠
Nature really knows how to put on a show.⁠
🎥: @horizonsalpins

Great spotted woodpeckers hammer trees at 40 strikes per second to find food and build nests, but that’s not all they use their beaks for. When nuts and acorns are tough to open, they can wedge them in tree bark and peck until shells crack to reach the food inside.

One of the world's rarest mammals is making a comeback 💚

The critically endangered Tenkile is found only in Papua New Guinea's Torricelli Mountains, where local communities have played a vital role in protecting this remarkable tree kangaroo. Seeing one caught on camera in the wild is a hopeful sign for its future! 

Discover this remarkable story in Wilderness with Simon Reeve, now streaming on BBC iPlayer. Link in bio 🔗

A young coati's first rule is simple: never lose sight of mum. But when a predator sends the family running for safety, one little pup is suddenly on its own.
